text:
jonah: Heads-up — saw a spike in p99 for EU (eu-1) over the last 20m. A non-trivial fraction of requests are being routed to us-west as a fallback which adds ~120ms. Affected tenants: platinum / enterprise. Also noticed model-variant fallbacks to lower-precision quant causing quality regressions.

maria: @jonah can you paste the logs or probe output? which health probe tripped? :eyes:

jonah: sample logs from 09:12 window:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:34Z route=eu-1 -> selected=us-west-2 latency=124ms probe=penalty=0.82 reason=capacity_shortfall
2026-03-18T09:12:34Z model_variant=redwood-ql-7b-q4 -> fallback=redwood-ql-7b-q8 quality_drop=0.14
```

kevin: :thinking_face: If we allow quant-fallback by default then routing can silently degrade quality for high-tier customers. We need a tier veto so platinum/orgs with SLAs never get auto-quant-fallback without opt-in.

liz: Agreed. Current routing decision only looks at latency + capacity_score. No tier-level policy. Proposal: add a tier policy layer that can veto variant-level fallbacks.

sam: Quick pseudocode for new policy block:
```
policy {
  route_priority: [local_region, same_continent, fallback]
  max_extra_latency_ms: 80
  tier_overrides {
    platinum: {allow_quant_fallback: false}
    enterprise: {allow_quant_fallback: true}
  }
}
```

maria: Also we need richer telemetry. Important fields: route_decision_reason, selected_variant, previous_variant, quality_delta, quota_bucket. Console should expose `routing.breakdown_by_tier` and `variant.quality_regressions`.

jonah: +1 on telemetry. UX idea: on the request details page, show a small "Why routed" tooltip that lists the decision chain (probes, capacity, tier override). Helps support teams diagnose.

kevin: For rollouts: admins should be able to toggle model_variant fallback per-customer org in the console. Eg: org-level flag `allow_experimental_quant` and a global default. That avoids surprise regressions.

liz: And add a graceful-degradation strategy: soft-affinity TTL (default 30s) before widening region selection, plus weighted-probing where penalties decay over time. That prevents flapping.

sam: Ran a quick sim last night. With soft-affinity TTL=30s and max_extra_latency=100ms we reduced cross-region failover by ~60%, p95 in eu improved by ~30ms, cost delta +4%. Detailed sim log attached in my PR.

jonah: Action items and owners:
- kevin: implement tier veto in routing engine (add allow_quant_fallback flag)
- maria: add telemetry schema + console widgets for routing/variant metrics
- sam: run region-wide sims across all active workloads and publish report
- liz: design console opt-in UI for per-org variant control + tooltip copy
Target: PRs open by EOD Thu, monitoring on for 24h post-canary.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout started: routing-engine v2.3.1 -> 5% traffic in eu region at 2026-03-18T12:05:00Z

kevin: Draft PR created (internal link). Tests: will include tier veto unit tests + e2e sim harness. @maria will need new telemetry fields added to schema before merging.

maria: I'll add the telemetry event names and dimension list by EOD today and ping infra for retention. Proposed events: `routing.decision`, `variant.fallback`, `variant.quality_delta`.

jonah: Thanks. We'll monitor `routing.breakdown_by_tier` and `variant.quality_regressions` for 24h. If quality_regressions > 0.1 (delta) for any platinum org, auto-disable quant fallback for that org and open a P1.

liz: :thumbsup:

jonah: filing follow-up doc for rollout checklist and console copy. Will circle back after the canary results.
